Chan Master Wen of Henan realized the principle of the threefold wisdom within the single mind taught by Nāgārjuna.
He expounded the oral instructions on the three contemplations for Chan Master Si.
Emperor Wen of the Chen dynasty...
At Mount Dasu, Master Si expounded the Four Practices for Peaceful Joy to Master Yi and showed him the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra’s place of practice.
[Emperor Wu] abolished the imperial throne.
Master Si came to reside at Mount Nanyue.
Bestowing the Precepts for Lord Yue. Emperor Xuan:
Master Zhiyi at Waguan Monastery in Jinling expounded the title of the Lotus Sūtra for Shen Junli, the Yitong. Emperor Shaodi.
The Emperor issued an edict for the Dhyāna Master of Waguan to attend the Taicheng Hall.
He opened the lectures on the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* and the *Ratnaketuparivarta-sūtra*. The Emperor issued an edict for the Dhyāna Master of Waguan to reside at Guangzhai Monastery.

The Emperor visited the temple to listen to the lecture on the *Renwang jing* (Benevolent Kings Sūtra). Dharma Master Guangzhai lectured on the *Fahua jing* (Lotus Sūtra), and Dharma Master Zhiyan of Zhang’an attended the lectures in advance.
This was during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Sui dynasty.
Prince Jin Wang Guang welcomed the Dhyāna Master to Yangzhou and conferred the Bodhisattva precepts upon him, bestowing on the Master the title "Zhi-zhe" (The Wise One).
Zhi-zhe Dhyāna Master conferred the Bodhisattva precepts upon Guan Yu and his son at Mount Yuquan. At Mount Yuquan, Zhi-zhe expounded the *Fahua xuanyi* (The Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra).
Zhang’an Listens in Advance: While Zhizhe was expounding the *Mohe zhiguan* at Yuquan Mountain, Zhang’an listened in advance. Emperor Gong:
At Tiantai Guoqing Temple, Zhang’an expounded the *Zhiguan* for Master Fahua Wei.
Emperor Gaozong of the Tang dynasty:
Tiangong Weicun Chan Master expounded *Zhi Guan* for him. Empress Wu:
Tiangong expounded *Zhi Guan* for Zuoxi Liangchan Master. Emperor Xuanzong: [Tiangong expounded *Zhi Guan* for him.]
Zuoxi lectured on the *Zhiguan* for Chan Master Ran of Jingxi during the reign of Emperor Daizong.
Jingxi lectured on the *Zhiguan* for Master Suí at Fulong during the reign of Emperor Dezong.
During the reign of Emperor Wenzong, Dharma Master Suì expounded the *Śamatha-vipaśyanā* for Dharma Master Xiū at Guoqing Temple.
During the reign of Emperor Xizong, Dharma Master Xiū expounded the *Śamatha-vipaśyanā* for Dharma Master Wài at Chanlin Temple.
The Master Wai preached *Zhi-guan* at Guoqing Temple for the Dharma Master Xiu.
During the Zhaozong era, the Dharma Master Xiu preached *Zhi-guan* at Guoqing Temple for the Dharma Master Song.
Emperor Gaozu of the Jin dynasty [invited] Dharma Master Song to Guoqing Temple, where he expounded *śamatha-vipaśyanā* (calm abiding and insight) for Dharma Master Ji.
Emperor Taizu of the Song dynasty...
Master Ji expounded the various dharma-gates of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā* to Master Tong at Luoxi;
Emperor Taizong [recorded this].
Master Tong, in turn, expounded the various dharma-gates of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā* to Master Li at Baoyun.
In the True Sect (Shinshū),
the Dharma Master Li was honored at Nanhu; he answered the inquiries of the Japanese Dharma Master Enchin,
and the imperial edict conferred the name "Yanqing" upon Ba'en.
Dongyi Wenshi composed two pieces of admonitory oaths to establish this as a place for the long-term lecturing on the Tiantai teachings.
Master Li organized a group of ten monks to perform the Lotus Repentance for three years.
He burned his own body as an offering to the Dharma.

Yan Shi of the Hanlin Academy sent a letter urging him to remain in this world. An imperial edict bestowed upon him four thousand six hundred and twenty fascicles of the printed texts of the teachings of the Zhiyi School from the Eastern Palace. Li Zunxu, the Commandant of the Household Cavalry, submitted a memorial.
The Fourth Ming Emperor praised the high conduct and self-sacrifice of Master Fashi,
bestowing upon him the title Fazhi. He then issued an imperial decree dispatching the inner attendant Yu Yuanqing.
He traveled to Yanqing in Siming to invite Fazhi to lead the assembly in performing repentance rites for the blessing of the realm;
he composed the "Essential Principles of Performing Repentance" for this purpose. Empress Dowager Zhangyi dispatched an envoy to India.
He invited Master Shishi to perform repentance rites for the sake of the state;
the Master then presented the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-rāja-sūtra* Ritual for Protecting the Nation.
He submitted a memorial requesting that the Tiantai doctrinal volumes be included in the Great Canon.
Emperor Renzong issued an imperial decree ordering the eunuch Yang Huagu to travel to Tianzhu Temple to pray for the blessing of the state.
Shi Fashi further petitioned for the inclusion of Tiantai doctrinal texts in the Tripitaka.
At the Buddha’s birthday, Fayi of Yanqing released fish and birds and composed the "Text on Releasing Living Beings."
The Prefectural Governor, Zeng Hui, reported this matter to the throne.
An imperial edict was issued for Liu Yun of the Bureau of Military Affairs to compose a text to be inscribed on a stone tablet erected at the temple gate.
Regarding Yanqing’s Fazhi, he opened the curtain to examine his students, a practice known as "kaivi" (opening the screen).
The Forty-two Sections Sutra remains a teaching to this day; an imperial edict was issued to include the Tiantai doctrinal texts in the Tripitaka;
a thousand members of the assembly at Mount Ling were provided with a vegetarian meal; and on Mount Dongye, Dharma Master Ru convened a hundred monks to perform the Long Repentance ritual.
Duwei Ma Zunxu reported this to the court,
whereupon he was granted the title "Divine Illumination" (Shenzhao),
along with the Prefect Zhang Dexiang and other worthies.
Establishment of the White Lotus Society:
During the reign of Emperor Shenzong, National Master Haimyue Huibian resided at Ling Shan on Mount Tiantai;
he was appointed by the Prefecture as the Head Monk (Du Sengzheng).
Whenever there was a vacant seat at a temple within the jurisdiction, all the eminent scholars from various monasteries were convened for a formal examination on doctrinal principles (*yìkē*).
Their names were recorded and they were subjected to rigorous evaluation. (Emperor Xiaozong).
An Imperial Decree for Dongchan Monastery in Fuzhou:

In accordance with the decree issued in the second year of the Tianzheng era, the scriptural sections of the Tiantai school were carved onto printing blocks and included in the Tripitaka. — Emperor Ningzong.
A Memorial from Jingmen Commandery Requesting the Enfeoffment of Yuzhan Zhi as a Master of Spiritual Wisdom.
Imperial Edict Granting the Title of Grand Master of Spiritual Wisdom.
Submitted by Shouyu of Lingshan during the reign of Emperor Lizong.
The *Ji-chao* (Excerpts) in more than two hundred fascicles, composed by the Great Master Fazhi, was requested for inclusion in the Imperial Canon;
this was granted.
Regarding the *Chanyuan Chuandeng* (Lamp of the Zen Garden): the *Chanyuan Chuandeng* [was compiled] during the first year of the Datong era of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty.
Bodhidharma crossed the sea and arrived at Guangzhou.
By imperial decree, he was summoned for an audience.
The Emperor asked, "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths?"
The Master said,
"Vast and open, there is no sage.
The Emperor said:
"Who is it facing me?
The Master replied,
"I do not know."
The Emperor did not accord with him.
The Master crossed the Yangtze River and entered Wei.
This was the first year of the Wuchai era of Xiaoming of the Northern Wei.
Bodhidharma entered Wei from Liang and stayed at Shaolin on Mount Songgao, facing a wall;
he did not respond to three imperial summons. This was the first year of the Dàtǒng era of Emperor Wén.
Dharma transmitted the Dharma and the kashaya to Huìkě;
he then sat upright and entered parinirvāṇa.
He was buried at Dinglin Monastery on Mount Xionger.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Sui dynasty,
the Second Patriarch Huik’e first transmitted the Dharma to Sengcan.
He went to Zhengchisi Temple to preach the Dharma.
There was a Dharma Master He who slandered the community with unlawful acts.
He previously said to Sengcan:
"I have karmic debts from past lives which I must now repay. [Emperor Yang].
The Third Patriarch, Sengcan, resided at Mount Wangong and transmitted the Dharma to the śrāmaṇera Daoxin;
he passed away while standing upright.
During the reign of Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty, the Fourth Patriarch Daoxin resided at Mount Huangmei;
though summoned four times, he did not rise [to accept office]. The Fourth Patriarch resided at Mount Poutou.
There was an old monk named Zaisong Daozhe (The Pine-Planting Wayfarer).
He was born as the daughter of the Zhou family,
but upon meeting the Fourth Patriarch, he was ordained as a monk.
This was Hongren, the Fourth Patriarch. From Mount Pòtóu,
a purple vapor rose like a canopy,
beneath which white vapors split into six paths.
Ren said,
"Might you not one day produce a separate branch of the Buddha-dharma?
The Patriarch replied, "I might."
Thus it was with Gaozong. When the Fifth Patriarch,
Hongren, saw the verse inscribed on the wall by the practitioner Huineng,
he summoned Neng at night and told him:
The Buddha has transmitted the treasury of the true Dharma-eye from one to another in succession;
I now transmit it to you, along with the robe that has been passed down,
to serve as a token of faith.
Huineng was able to travel south all night;
the following morning, the Elder [Hui]neng pursued him as far as Yuling,
where Huineng cast his robe and bowl onto a rock.
It is clearly stated that he was unmoved by such honors, and so forth.

Emperor Gaozong [bestowed honors upon] Chan Master Rong of Niutou, who had received the Dharma from the Fifth Patriarch and fulfilled the prophecy of producing a separate branch of the Buddha-dharma. When Huineng arrived in Guangzhou, he encountered Chan Master Yinzong.
He shaved his head and received the precepts for him, extensively opening the Dharma-gate of Dongshan.
The following year, he returned to Caoxi. (Emperor) Zhongzong.
He dispatched an envoy to welcome the Sixth Patriarch to the capital to propagate the Way,
but the Patriarch declined the invitation on the grounds of illness.
Emperor Suzong then issued an imperial decree for an envoy to go to Shaoshan to receive the Sixth Patriarch’s robe and bowl.
Upon entering the inner palace to offer worship,
Emperor Daizong dreamed that the Sixth Patriarch requested the return of his robe and bowl to the mountain.
He issued an imperial decree for Liu Jing to carry them back on his head and deliver them there.
The Emperor issued an edict for National Teacher Zhong to have an audience.
He asked him, "Do you recognize the mountain?
Do you recognize the land?"
[The Master] was literate and skilled in calculation, and so forth.
Emperor Xianzong [asked about this]. Li Bo, the Prefectural Governor of Jiangzhou, asked Chan Master Chang of Guizong:

When he was first born,

but it shall be revived thanks to you."

On the *gengzi* day of the eleventh month in the twenty-first year of King Ling of Zhou, Confucius was born in the town of Zou in Lu. [This occurred] in the tenth year of King Jing.

he served as the magistrate of Zhongdu in Lu.

There he edited the *Shi*, finalized the *Shu*, appended the hexagrams of the *Zhou Yi*, and composed the *Chunqiu*.

He had three thousand disciples,

In the fourth year of the Tianjian era of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty.

In the eleventh year of the Zhenguan era of Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty,
according to the established regulations for the ritual of *shidian*,

Confucius had been regarded as the "First Teacher" (xianshi).

"The state of Liang perished because its people practiced fasting and abstinence; this was not the fault of Śākyamuni. The above constitutes the explanation of the Buddhist teaching.

where is my mind? He asked this three times, and each time his question was verified.
The Master questioned her again.
The woman’s arguments were exhausted,
and she transformed into a female fox.
He descended the steps and fled.

Observing the discussions among the three teachings,

He commissioned the Court Doctor Xu Kuang, the Śramaṇa Huìchéng, and the Daoist Liu Jìnshàn to provide exegesis. Emperor Taizong issued an edict appointing the Director of the National Academy Kǒng Yǐngdá, the Śramaṇa Huìjìng, and the Daoist Cài Huáng [to do the same].

Entering Hongwen Hall to discuss the Three Teachings: By imperial decree, the Palace Secretariat Official Xu Yue, the Śramaṇa Tan Yan, and the Daoist Ge Chancheng were ordered to lecture and debate on the Three Teachings.
By imperial decree, the Śramaṇa Duānfǔ was also appointed.
